deferred: All six previously unlinked named-place assessments now include external research. Bibliographic gaps in this declared batch are addressed at the stated scope; exact identifications, comparative excavation review, textual variants and abstract-only access remain unresolved. Regional placeholders were not upgraded.

The other 87 explained pairs retain their existing review labels and have no new source-level assessment in these batches. Many assessed pairs still need fuller academic literature, textual and specialist review.
Other person-trail access gaps, full excavation reports, manuscript apparatuses, wider source coverage and independent specialist review remain open.
The full OpenBible corpus remains unclassified.

records.title: 2 Samuel 7:12-16 and Luke 1:26-33
records.note: Luke's annunciation describes David's throne and an enduring kingdom, recalling the dynastic promise in Samuel.
records.limitation: Retain echo, not direct quotation. Samuel's immediate dynastic setting and Luke's application should not be flattened into one speech. Additional independent academic literature was not assessed for this pair in this batch.

records.title: Exodus 16:1-8 and John 6:30-35
records.note: John explicitly discusses manna and distinguishes Moses from the Father as giver, before presenting Jesus as the bread of life.
records.limitation: Retain the thematic label for these anchors; typological interpretation is possible. records.title: Psalm 2:6-9 and Hebrews 1:1-9
records.note: Hebrews cites Psalm 2:7 as part of a sequence distinguishing the Son from angels; the psalm presents royal sonship.
records.limitation: The surrounding sequence also cites 2 Samuel 7:14. This check does not independently settle historical royal identity or later Trinitarian debates.

records.title: Isaiah 53:4-6 and 1 Peter 2:21-25
records.note: First Peter uses Isaiah's suffering-servant language and directly quotes the healing-through-wounds clause in an exhortation about suffering and righteous conduct.
records.limitation: Classify this pair as quotation rather than a merely possible echo. The pastoral context does not license endorsing abuse or promising automatic physical cure. Additional independent academic literature was not assessed for this pair in this batch.

records.title: Jeremiah 31:31-34 and Luke 22:14-20
records.note: Luke's cup saying uses new-covenant language associated with Jeremiah, in a meal setting that also invokes sacrificial blood.
records.limitation: Classify as echo rather than a direct quotation of Jeremiah's full promise. Compare Exodus 24:8 and textual variants of Luke's supper account before broader claims. Additional independent academic literature was not assessed for this pair in this batch.
